2027-03-04.title: Thursday of the fourth week of the Great Fast
readings: Hagar and Ishmael are sent away; God promises to make a nation of the boy
Knowledge puffs up, but love builds up
Love your enemies; be perfect as your heavenly Father is perfect
2027-03-04.verse: But I say to you, Love your enemies and pray for those who persecute you,
theo: Today's first reading is painful. At the feast for Isaac, Sarah sees Ishmael, Hagar's son, playing with her son and demands: “Cast out this slave woman with her son; for the son of this slave woman shall not inherit along with my son Isaac.” Scripture is honest: “The matter was very distressing to Abraham on account of his son.” Ishmael was his child too. God tells Abraham that the line of promise will run through Isaac, but he does not forget the other boy: “As for the son of the slave woman, I will make a nation of him also, because he is your offspring.” Abraham rises early, puts bread and a skin of water on Hagar's shoulder, and sends her into the wilderness of Beer-sheba. This is a family torn apart by jealousy and fear of losing an inheritance, the kind of quarrel that still divides homes over land and property. Yet God's care reaches beyond the walls of Abraham's tent. The boy who is sent away is not sent away from God.

Paul gives the Corinthians a principle that would have helped Abraham's household: “Knowledge puffs up, but love builds up.” The Christians of Corinth knew that idols are nothing and that “there is no God but one,” and some were using that knowledge to look down on weaker believers. Paul corrects them: “anyone who loves God is known by him.” What matters is not how much I know but whether I build others up. St Augustine summed up the whole Christian life in a short line: love, and do what you will; for if the root within is love, nothing but good can grow from it (in substance). Jesus takes love to its furthest point: “You have heard that it was said, ‘You shall love your neighbor and hate your enemy.’ But I say to you, Love your enemies and pray for those who persecute you, so that you may be children of your Father in heaven; for he makes his sun rise on the evil and on the good.” The Father does not ration his sunshine according to merit. In this Great Fast we are asked to imitate that generosity: to pray for those who wrong us, and to greet those whom we would rather avoid. “Be perfect, therefore, as your heavenly Father is perfect.”
outline: Ask: has jealousy or an inheritance ever divided a family you know?
Point 1 · The boy who was sent away
Abraham's distress and God's promise to Ishmael.
The sun on the evil and the good.
“Love your enemies and pray for those who persecute you.”
live: Name before God one person who has hurt you or works against you, and pray for his or her good every day of this week.
Build up, do not puff up (1 Corinthians 8:1)
Today, instead of correcting or showing what you know, say one word that encourages a person who is weak or struggling.
2027-03-04.prayer: Heavenly Father, you make your sun rise on the evil and on the good and send rain on the righteous and the unrighteous. You did not forget the boy who was sent into the wilderness. Heal the jealousy and quarrels that divide our families. Keep us from the knowledge that puffs up, and fill us with the love that builds up. Give us grace in this Great Fast to love our enemies and pray for those who persecute us, so that we may be your children and grow perfect as you are perfect. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.
altar: At the altar Christ offers himself for friends and enemies alike; the love that prayed “Father, forgive them” becomes our food in the Holy Qurbono.

quick: Sarah demanded that Hagar and Ishmael be sent away; Abraham was distressed, and God promised to make a nation of the boy.
Knowledge puffs up, but love builds up; there is one God, the Father, and one Lord, Jesus Christ.
Jesus commands us to love our enemies and pray for those who persecute us, as the Father is generous to all.
2027-03-04.action: Pray today, by name, for someone who has hurt you.
2027-03-04.question: Whom am I keeping outside the tent of my love?

family.explain: Jesus says something very hard: love your enemies and pray for people who are mean to you. Why? Because God is like that. He lets the sun shine on good people and bad people. When we are kind to someone who is not kind to us, we are acting like God's children.
family.intention: We pray for someone who has been unkind to us.
family.ask: Ask: “Is there someone we find hard to love? Can we pray for them together tonight?”

illus: Two brothers in a village near Kottayam stopped speaking after their father's death, over a strip of rubber land on the boundary. For six years they passed each other at church without a word. During one Great Fast the younger brother's wife fell ill and was admitted to hospital. The older brother heard of it at the Wednesday prayer meeting. That evening he went to the hospital, sat outside the ward for a long time, and finally went in with a flask of kanji. He did not mention the land. Neither did his brother. The strip is still there, and so are the brothers, on speaking terms.

pm.open: Father in heaven, you love the good and the evil alike. Make our hearts like yours. Amen.
share: The matter was very distressing to Abraham on account of his son (Genesis 21:11). Where has jealousy or fear of loss caused pain in my family?
Knowledge puffs up, but love builds up (1 Corinthians 8:1). Do I use what I know to build others up or to feel superior?
Love your enemies and pray for those who persecute you (Matthew 5:44). Whom is Jesus asking me to pray for today?
pm.resp: Lord, teach us to love as you love.
interc: For families divided by property disputes and inheritance.
For mothers and children who have been abandoned or sent away.
For our enemies and for those who persecute Christians.
For teachers and the learned, that their knowledge may serve love.
For the children of Abraham, Jews, Christians and Muslims, that they may live in peace.
pm.close: Father, you are perfect in love. Heal our divisions, turn our knowledge into service, and give us courage to love those who hate us, so that we may truly be your children. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

homily: Dear friends, in the first reading a family is torn apart. Sarah says: cast out this slave woman with her son. The matter was very distressing to Abraham on account of his son (Genesis 21:10–11). Jealousy and fear of losing an inheritance still divide many families.
But God does not forget Ishmael: as for the son of the slave woman, I will make a nation of him also, because he is your offspring (Genesis 21:13). God's care reaches the one who is sent away.
Paul tells us: knowledge puffs up, but love builds up; anyone who loves God is known by him (1 Corinthians 8:1, 3). Knowing many things is not enough; we must build others up.

And Jesus says: love your enemies and pray for those who persecute you, so that you may be children of your Father in heaven; for he makes his sun rise on the evil and on the good (Matthew 5:44–45). In this Fast, let us pray for one person we find hard to love. Amen.
kids: Children, Jesus asks us to do something very brave: to love even people who are not nice to us, and to pray for them. God makes the sun shine on everyone, good and bad. Tonight, can you pray for someone who was unkind to you? That makes you look like God's own child.

intro: Theme: “Love your enemies and pray for those who persecute you.”
A family torn by jealousy, the knowledge that puffs up and the love that builds up, and the Father's generous sun.

points.h: The boy who was sent away
q: As for the son of the slave woman, I will make a nation of him also, because he is your offspring.
So it is not the will of your Father in heaven that one of these little ones should be lost.
points.apply: Reach out this week to one relative from whom your family has been divided.

q: Hatred stirs up strife, but love covers all offenses.
Love is patient; love is kind; love is not envious or boastful or arrogant
points.apply: Each day this week say one sincere word of encouragement to someone who is struggling.

sub: The old saying and the new command.
Sun on the evil and the good.
q: If your enemies are hungry, give them bread to eat; and if they are thirsty, give them water to drink;
Do not be overcome by evil, but overcome evil with good.
points.apply: Do one concrete act of kindness this week for someone who has wronged you.

concl: God's care reaches beyond our family quarrels to the one who is sent away.
The love that prays for enemies makes us children of the Father.
2027-03-04.resolve: Pray daily for one enemy until Easter, and let love, not knowledge, rule your words.
